/tools/gas-finder.title: Cheapest Gas Finder — Counts the Gas Used to Get There
/tools/gas-finder.description: Find the cheapest place to fill up near you. Pick your car and how full the tank is, and nearby stations are ranked by the true cost of a fill-up including the gas burned driving there. Free, no sign-up.
/tools/gas-finder.keywords: cheapest gas near me, gas price finder, is it worth driving for cheaper gas, gas calculator, fuel cost calculator, gas station finder, mpg calculator, cheap gas

application.name: Cheapest Gas Finder
featureList: Year, make and model lookup for about 19,000 vehicles from EPA data
Separate MPG for every engine, transmission and drivetrain, about 29,000 in all
An estimated tank size for every vehicle, editable along with MPG
Fuel gauge slider for how full the tank is right now
Finds gas stations up to 50 miles from your location or a ZIP code
Ranks stations by the full cost of the fill-up including the drive there and back
Add a destination to find the cheapest stop along the way, counting only the detour
Flags when the lowest sign price is not actually the cheapest option
Regular, midgrade, premium and diesel
One-tap directions to the winning station

faq.q: Is it worth driving farther for cheaper gas?
faq.a: Usually only when the station is close. Every extra mile burns gas at the price you are trying to save on. A 5¢ discount on 11 gallons saves 55¢, while an extra 16 miles of round trip in a 25 mpg car burns about $3 of gas. This tool does that math for every nearby station.

faq.q: Where do the MPG numbers come from?
faq.a: From the U.S. EPA's fueleconomy.gov dataset, using the combined city and highway rating. Each engine, transmission and drivetrain has its own rating, so a 2020 Camaro with the 2.0L turbo and automatic shows 25 mpg while the 6.2L V8 shows 20. Pick yours from the engine list. If you know your real-world MPG, type it in instead.

link.text: Download the EPA fuel economy dataset

faq.q: Why is the tank size marked as an estimate?
faq.a: The EPA doesn't publish fuel tank capacity, and no open dataset does, so it's estimated from the vehicle's size class and from the tank it would need for a typical highway range. It's usually within a gallon or two. Your owner's manual will have the exact figure. Type it in and the results update.

faq.q: Where do the gas prices come from?
faq.a: Where live prices are available, they come from Google's station listings, for up to 3 searches a day per device. Any station without a listed price can be filled in with the price you see on the sign, and it is ranked straight away.

faq.q: Can it find the cheapest gas on the way somewhere?
faq.a: Yes. Add a destination and it looks for stations along the route instead of around you. The drive itself costs the same wherever you stop, so each station is charged only for the detour it adds: out to the station and back to your route. A station right on your way adds nothing, so a cheaper one has to be close to the route to win.

faq.q: Is my location stored anywhere?
faq.a: Not by this site. To find stations and measure driving distances, your location and destination are sent to the services that do the lookup: OpenStreetMap's servers (station list, address search and OSRM routing) and Google Maps (prices and backup routing). Nothing is saved on a server here. Your car and settings are remembered in your own browser so you don't have to pick them again; use Start over to forget them.

faq.q: How are driving distances worked out?
faq.a: With a routing service that follows real roads: OpenStreetMap's OSRM, with Google's routing as a backup. On a trip, a stop costs the drive from your start to the station and on to your destination, minus the drive you'd make anyway. If neither service answers, distances are estimated from a straight line and marked with ≈ so you can tell.

/seating-chart.title: Free Wedding Seating Chart Maker — Drag & Drop, No Sign-Up
/seating-chart.description: Plan your wedding reception seating in your browser. Add round or rectangular tables, import your guest list, drag everyone into a seat, then export a PNG, CSV, or JSON. Free, no sign-up, nothing leaves your device.
/seating-chart.keywords: wedding seating chart, seating chart maker, free seating chart, reception table planner, wedding table layout, guest list seating, seating chart template, drag and drop seating chart, wedding planning tool
/seating-chart.imageAlt: A wedding seating chart being arranged, with round tables and named guest seats

application.name: Wedding Seating Chart Maker
featureList: Round, oval, square, and rectangular tables
Import a guest list from CSV or pasted text
Drag and drop guests into seats
Swap two guests by dropping one onto the other
Rename, reshape, and resize tables on a zoomable floor plan
Export a PNG floor plan, a CSV seat list, or a JSON table listing
Saves automatically in your browser with no account

faq.q: Is this wedding seating chart maker really free?
faq.a: Yes. It is completely free, there is no account to create, and there is no limit on guests or tables.

faq.q: Does my guest list get uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. The chart is built entirely in your browser and saved in your browser's local storage. Your guest list is never sent to a server.

faq.q: Can I import my guest list from a spreadsheet?
faq.a: Yes. Export your guests as a CSV and use Import CSV file, or paste names straight into the paste box — one name per line, or columns named First and Last, or a single Name column.

faq.q: How do I save my seating chart and come back to it later?
faq.a: The chart saves itself in the browser you are using, so you can close the tab and return to it. To move it to another device or keep a backup, use Download JSON and load that file later with Load JSON.

faq.q: What can I export when the seating chart is finished?
faq.a: Three formats: a PNG image of the floor plan to print or send to your venue, a CSV listing every seat for your caterer, and a JSON file listing each table with the names of the guests seated at it.

faq.q: Can I use it for something other than a wedding?
faq.a: Yes. Nothing is wedding specific — it works just as well for banquets, galas, classrooms, conferences, or any event where you need to assign people to tables.

faq.q: Is this sales order generator free?
faq.a: Yes. There is no account, no watermark, no limit on line items, and no paid tier.

faq.q: Does my customer data get uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. The sheet is built entirely in your browser and the draft is saved in your browser's local storage. Nothing is sent to a server.

faq.q: What is the difference between a sales order and an invoice?
faq.a: A sales order confirms what the customer has agreed to buy before it ships, so it carries a ship-to address, weights and a ship date. An invoice asks for payment after the fact, so it carries payment terms, a due date and a balance due. Use the invoice generator for the second half of the job.

faq.q: Can I load an order from my own system?
faq.a: Yes. Open the JSON panel and paste a payload. Keys you do not recognise are ignored, and older key names such as items, price and shipto are still accepted.

faq.q: Will my draft still be here tomorrow?
faq.a: Yes, as long as you use the same browser and do not clear your site data. To move an order elsewhere or keep a backup, download it as JSON and paste it back in later.

faq.q: Does this work with NetSuite?
faq.a: Not directly — it does not connect to NetSuite. The layout mirrors a NetSuite sales order print, so it is a quick way to settle on a design before you build the equivalent Advanced PDF template in FreeMarker.
